name: Camera
aliases: can i bring camera on plane
カメラ 機内持ち込み
description: Guidelines for traveling with cameras, lenses, and batteries in your luggage.

carryOn.reason: Cameras, lenses, and camera bodies are 100% permitted in carry-on baggage. Carrying fragile optics and expensive electronics in the cabin is strongly recommended to prevent damage, theft, and baggage handler impact.
conditions: Spare lithium-ion camera batteries must remain in carry-on baggage only.

checkedBag.reason: Cameras are technically allowed in checked luggage, but airlines and security agencies strongly recommend keeping valuable cameras and delicate lenses in carry-on baggage. Any spare lithium-ion batteries are strictly forbidden in checked bags.
conditions: Spare lithium-ion camera batteries are prohibited in checked luggage.

tsa.pageTitle: Can I bring camera on a plane?

airlines.name: Korean Air
airlines.notes: Digital cameras permitted in carry-on and checked luggage. Korean aviation safety regulations strictly prohibit spare lithium camera batteries in checked luggage — all spare batteries must be carried in cabin baggage.

airlines.name: Asiana Airlines
airlines.notes: Cameras and optical lenses permitted in carry-on baggage. Spare camera batteries must be carried in hand luggage with terminals protected from short circuit.

airlines.name: Japan Airlines (JAL)
airlines.notes: Cameras permitted in cabin baggage. Cabin carriage recommended for high-value equipment. Lithium-ion batteries must meet IATA safety limits (under 100Wh).

airlines.name: ANA (All Nippon Airways)
airlines.notes: Cameras permitted in carry-on and checked bags. Passengers are advised to carry delicate cameras and lenses as carry-on baggage.

airlines.name: Delta Air Lines
airlines.notes: Cameras, lenses, and camcorders permitted in carry-on and checked bags. Cabin baggage recommended for fragile optical gear.

South Korea.reason: South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) allows cameras in both carry-on and checked bags. MOLIT aviation safety rules strictly mandate that spare lithium-ion batteries must be in carry-on luggage only. Hand inspection is available for analog film at Incheon and Gimpo security checkpoints.

Japan.reason: Japan Civil Aviation Bureau (JCAB) and Japan Customs permit cameras in carry-on and checked luggage. Cabin carriage recommended for expensive cameras. Photographers traveling with analog film can request manual hand inspection at security to avoid CT scan fogging.

UK.reason: UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) permits cameras in carry-on and checked bags. Spare batteries must be kept in cabin baggage.

Australia.reason: CASA allows cameras in carry-on and checked baggage. Spare lithium batteries must be packed in carry-on luggage.

travelTips: Always keep your camera body, high-end lenses, and memory cards in your carry-on luggage or personal item to avoid theft or rough baggage handling.
Spare lithium-ion camera batteries MUST be packed in your carry-on luggage — never pack loose spare batteries in checked luggage.
Request a manual hand-check for analog photographic film at airport security to avoid exposure to high-intensity CT scanners.
Remove heavy telephoto lenses from camera bodies before stowing your bag in overhead compartments to prevent lens mount strain.
Travel tripods and monopods under 60 cm (24 inches) folded are generally permitted in carry-on bags; check your airline's maximum dimensions.

faq.question: Is camera allowed in carry-on bags?
faq.answer: Camera is allowed in carry-on luggage. Cameras are fully allowed in carry-on bags. Keep fragile lenses and camera bodies in your cabin baggage to prevent damage or theft.

faq.question: Can you pack camera in checked baggage?
faq.answer: Yes, Camera is allowed in checked bags. Cameras are allowed in checked baggage, but carrying them in the cabin is strongly recommended to protect delicate electronics.

ruleHistory.change: Added Korean Air, Asiana, JAL airline rules, spare battery safety rules, and film scanner guidance.
